f.title: Centralised, risk-based monitoring may be used to detect regional differences in adverse event reporting
f.statement: Centralised and risk-based monitoring may be particularly useful for MRCTs in order to monitor and mitigate the impact of emerging regional differences in, for example, trial subject retention or adverse event reporting.
f.clause: 2.1.2 Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Requirements and MRCTs
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Quality system & CAPA

f.title: Describe and justify in the protocol how regional variation in AE reporting used as endpoints will be minimised
f.statement: Where variables such as certain adverse events may show regional differences in reporting patterns due to cultural variation rather than true differences in incidence, their use as endpoints in MRCTs will require careful planning, and approaches to minimise the impact of this variation on data collection and interpretation of the trial results should be described and justified in the study protocol.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

Use of these variables as endpoints in MRCTs will require careful planning. Approaches to minimise the impact of this variation in data collection and interpretation of the trial results should be described and justified in the study protocol.

f.title: Standardise efficacy and safety information and investigator training across participating regions
f.statement: Methods of collecting and handling efficacy and safety information should be standardised across participating regions. It is also important to provide standardised training for investigators and study personnel in each region before initiating the trial in that region, so that the trial objectives are met through standardised implementation of the study protocol.
f.clause: 2.2.6 Collecting and Handling of Efficacy and Safety Information
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

f.title: Conduct safety reporting per ICH E2 and also adhere locally to differing local requirements
f.statement: Safety reporting should be conducted in accordance with ICH E2. When local regulations specify different requirements, such as timelines and criteria for expedited reporting, these should also be adhered to locally.
f.clause: 2.2.6 Collecting and Handling of Efficacy and Safety Information

f.title: Consider a committee able to assess trial context to monitor accumulating efficacy and safety information in MRCTs
f.statement: Use of a committee able to adequately assess the context of the trial should be considered, in order to monitor the accumulating efficacy and/or safety information from the MRCT while maintaining the integrity of the ongoing trial.
f.clause: 2.2.6 Collecting and Handling of Efficacy and Safety Information

f.title: Centralised, risk-based monitoring may be used to identify regional variability in adverse event reporting
f.statement: Centralised and risk-based monitoring may be particularly useful for MRCTs to identify variability across regions and sites in protocol compliance (e.g., differences in follow-up, compliance with study medications, adverse event reporting).
f.clause: 2.2.6 Collecting and Handling of Efficacy and Safety Information

f.title: Justify use of an unapproved active comparator in the protocol, including safety considerations
f.statement: Where an active comparator used in an MRCT is not approved in a participating region, the justification for its use, including safety considerations, should be described in the protocol based on scientific information.
